summary: Both fix_tasks discharged and mutation-proven: connect now runs outside the mutex with locked guards each side, and the pre-connect pause guard has exact, non-vacuous coverage.
notes: FACTS (orchestrator-owned, independently measured, not re-derived here): 30/30 contract verify commands exit 0; '--- PASS' = 84 (56 on main); go test ./internal/canal/ -count=1 -race -timeout 60s = ok in 1.826s, no race; quorum analyze contract-check with file_diffs = {ok:true, violations:[]}; 14 files, 1898 diff lines against a limit of 1900 (TWO lines of headroom).

MUTATION EVIDENCE (orchestrator, independent party). Round 2: deleting the terminal guard in procesarDesconexion kills TestSupervisorIgnoraParaSiempreLosEventosPosterioresAlBaneoTemporal. Closing round: replacing the pre-connect guard 'if pausada { registrarPausaVigente; return }' with '_ = pausada' makes TestSupervisorNoArrancaUnIntentoNuevoConLaPausaYaVigente the ONLY failing test in the package, in 0.00s. Both mutants restored byte-identical, green again. FIX B's test is therefore that guard's sole and exact coverage, and it fails fast rather than hanging.

FIX A - CRITICAL SECTION VERIFIED BY READING. reintentarConexion now takes mu, reads pausada and the conectar function pointer, releases mu (reconexion.go:292-295), calls conectar(ctx) unlocked (line 304), then re-acquires mu (308-313) to re-read pausada before acting on the result. Confirmed that s.mu.Unlock() precedes the conectar call and a fresh s.mu.Lock() follows it. Unbounded network I/O is no longer performed under the state lock, so the goroutine-leak-per-event hazard from round 2 is gone.

FIX A (1) - POST-CONNECT RE-CHECK IS SOUND ON THE STATE IT GUARDS. Nothing computed before the ban can be written after it for the two pieces of state that matter. 'intentos' is only reset (s.intentos = 0) inside the same critical section that reads pausada and only when !pausada && err == nil, so a ban that landed during the unlocked window suppresses the write. 'ultimoEstado' is written exclusively by emitirEstado, which is reached only after the post-connect pausada check returns false, so no 'activa' is written over a 'pausada' on the ordinary path. The single-policy reservation is NOT weakened by releasing mu: tomarPolitica/soltarPolitica is a separate flag taken on entry to reintentarConexion and released by defer on exit, so it is held for the ENTIRE call including the unlocked connect window; exactly one retry loop can exist regardless of mu. Mutation-proven in round 2 (deleting the reservation kills TestSupervisorNoAbreDosBuclesDeReconexionSimultaneos in 0.00s).

FIX A (2) - THE RESIDUAL-RACE COMMENT IS ACCURATE AND DOES NOT OVERCLAIM (reconexion.go:276-291). Each of its assertions checks out: the connect is deliberately outside the lock; ConnectContext carries no deadline and whatsmeow's websocket HTTP client is built with no Timeout field, so the upgrade is unbounded; holding mu across it would block entrarEnPausaTerminal, enPausa and emitirEstado, which are precisely the three methods that take mu, one leaked goroutine per event; a context deadline is NOT an available bound because whatsmeow adopts the dial context as the SESSION context (socket/framesocket.go:97-112 assigns fs.parentCtx = ctx and derives fs.cancelCtx from it), so a deadline would tear down the live session. The comment states the residual race plainly - at most ONE connect attempt can be in flight when the ban arrives - calls it irreducible because the ban is decided server-side, notes the previous design did not eliminate it either but merely traded it for unbounded lock retention, and limits its guarantee to what is actually guaranteed: once the ban is recorded, no NEW attempt ever starts. That is exactly what the code delivers, no more.

FIX B (3) - THE NEW TEST EXERCISES THE PRE-CONNECT GUARD AND NOTHING ADJACENT. The transient Disconnected enters the retry loop; the injected Espera, on the SAME goroutine and with mu released, processes a real TemporaryBan end to end (entrarEnPausaTerminal, emitirEstado, esperarBaneoTemporal, whose re-entry into Espera short-circuits on enPausa() and terminates at the declared expiry, so it cannot hang). Control then returns into the loop AFTER esperar, where the pre-connect guard is the only check standing between it and conectar - the top-of-loop guard belongs to the next iteration and is never reached. PRESENCE-BEFORE-ABSENCE IS REAL AND NON-VACUOUS: it first asserts two estados were emitted, the first 'reconectando' and the second 'pausada' carrying causa=baneo_temporal, the raw TempBanBlockedByUsers codigo and the converted ABSOLUTE expira_en_ms (ahoraFijoMs+1000+3000, validating the relative-to-absolute conversion at the advanced clock), and only then asserts conexiones == 0 and that EventoPausaVigente was logged. A supervisor that simply did nothing would fail the presence half, so the zero is a live zero. Single-goroutine, no channel handshake, no sync.Once - it cannot hang.

FIX B (3b) - COVERAGE IS EXACT. Under the guard's deletion the only assertion that trips is conexiones != 0: the estados pair and the EventoPausaVigente log are still produced by the post-connect re-check, so the test isolates precisely the behaviour the guard supplies (no NEW attempt starts) rather than passing for an incidental reason.

(4) INVARIANT SURVIVES: once a ban is recorded, no NEW connection attempt ever starts. Four independent barriers verified by reading: the top-of-loop guard before intentos++ (reconexion.go:254-259), the pre-connect guard (292-299, now covered), the post-connect re-check which returns instead of continuing the loop even when err != nil (308-317), and the terminal guard in procesarDesconexion (154-158, mutation-proven). entrarEnPausaTerminal returns false on a second ban and short-circuits to registrarPausaVigente without re-entering esperarBaneoTemporal. Grep confirms 's.pausada = true' at line 177 is the ONLY write in the entire module - the flag is unexported, one-way, and has no clearer, exported or internal - and all five reads occur under mu.

(4b) RESIDUAL, NOT INTRODUCED BY THIS DISCHARGE, NOT BLOCKING, AND NOT FIXABLE IN TWO LINES: between the post-connect unlock (line 313) and emitirEstado(activa) (line 331) there is a window two log calls wide in which a concurrently landing ban could emit 'pausada' first and have 'activa' emitted after it, inverting the status pair seen by the IPC consumer. It does NOT violate the stated invariant - the loop returns immediately after emitting and starts no further attempt, and any later event hits the terminal guard. It is pre-existing rather than new: the previous lock-across-connect design had the same inversion and arguably a wider window, since blocked ban goroutines were released at the same instant. It is also currently unobservable, as the IPC server consuming these states does not yet exist in this task (NuevoSupervisor still defaults a nil sumidero to a no-op). Closing it properly requires emitting the state inside the same critical section that reads pausada, which means a locked variant of emitirEstado - well beyond the two remaining diff lines. Recorded here so the task that builds the IPC server picks it up; deliberately NOT raised as a fix_task and nothing was trimmed to accommodate it.

(5) INVARIANTS RE-CONFIRMED AT CLOSING: all added comments and identifiers are in Spanish; the IPC message-type set is still NINE (9 'TipoMensaje = ' constants in internal/ipc/mensajes.go); the executable privacy guard TestElEventoEntranteNoTransportaNingunIdentificadorDeTransporte is intact in mensajes_test.go; no file under crates/, Cargo.*, .github/, docs/adr/, docs/plan/, docs/PRD.md, docs/bitacora-de-descartes.md or docs/runbook-restauracion-de-celula.md is touched - the changed set is docs/STATUS.md, docs/protocolo-ipc-nucleo-sidecar.md, sidecar/internal/canal/{canal.go,canal_test.go,reconexion.go,reconexion_interno_test.go,taxonomia_interno_test.go}, sidecar/internal/ipc/{documento_test.go,mensajes.go} and sidecar/main.go. The two new log events add no field to the closed registro.Campos struct and their detalle carries only closed-vocabulary causa values, no JID or credential material.

PRIOR ROUNDS CARRIED FORWARD (validated earlier, unchanged since): the taxonomy's closed causa vocabulary and its three-direction agreement with the protocol document; the OnConnect discriminator; the two independent backoff clamps ('siguiente > maximo' and the 'restante' ban clamp) each covered by its own case; the 'actual >= maximo' surviving mutant judged an EQUIVALENT mutant, subsumed by the next-iteration clamp for every parameter combination; the STATUS.md Pendiente entry naming all five HEXCELL_RETROCESO_* variables and marking the defaults pending calibration, which matches configuracion.go and section 5 of the protocol document.
ENVIRONMENT (unchanged, not a defect in this diff): the contract's verify commands do not export a writable GOCACHE, which the fleet sandbox needs. Worth carrying into the contract for future tasks.
DIFF HEADROOM: 1898 of 1900 lines used. No finding in this closing round requires a code change, so no contract amendment is needed.
